correctness.rationale: The explicit complete neighborhood-facet cover splits into two sphere-collapsible pieces whose exact intersection is connected Cr_n. For n>=4 both target pieces are simply connected, so every graph-to-piece attaching map is nullhomotopic and their cofibration pushout splits as two (n-2)-spheres plus the suspension of Cr_n, i.e. n^2-3n+1 two-spheres. The exact published Alexander dual identity on 2n vertices shifts integral degree j to cohomology degree 2n-j-3; this gives ranks, vanishing and no torsion. Exhaustive finite face identities and mod-two homology checks n=4..8 corroborate; finite field calculations are not used for the integral/all-n inference.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the canonical perfect-matching deletions from balanced complete bipartite graphs. Their exact dominance homology is a natural problem in the published Alexander-dual framework. The theorem supplies a uniform all-n topological classification of the complementary neighborhood complex and complete torsion-free integral homology of the crown dominance complex, with two distinct degrees for every n>=5 and a provable n=4 boundary merger. The explicit pushout explains the invariant rather than giving a coincidental small table. No stronger general result or equivariance is asserted.
